title: UNC3886
summary: UNC3886 is a China linked espionage cluster tracked by Mandiant that public reporting describes as targeting edge network appliances and virtualisation platforms, including devices in the telecommunications, technology, government and defence sectors. The cluster is notable for using zero day exploits, meaning flaws with no vendor fix at the time of the attack, against internet facing gateways, and for moving from those devices into the virtualisation layer where many workloads live. Reported tradecraft includes custom malware that runs on the appliance itself, rootkit style hiding, credential theft from device configuration, and tunnelling traffic through compromised devices. Because the targets are appliances, evidence is concentrated in device logs, firmware or configuration changes, and network flows rather than endpoint agents. Although the cluster is widely described as state linked and associated with China, such attribution rests on public reporting and is presented with varying confidence, and no named individuals are confirmed.

beginner.definition: UNC3886 is a group of spies that attacks the devices at the edge of a network. Edge devices are the machines that connect your network to the internet, such as firewalls and gateways. Public reports link this group to China.
beginner.whyItMatters: Edge devices sit in front of everything else. If an intruder controls one, they can watch traffic and slip inside without setting off alarms. Big virtual systems that run many servers are also a target, because one weakness there affects dozens of services. These cases often stay hidden for months before anyone notices.
howItWorks: They find an internet facing device with a flaw nobody has fixed yet.
They exploit the flaw and run their own code on the device.
They hide their changes so normal checks do not show them.
They steal stored passwords for other systems from the device.
They use the device to reach virtual servers inside the network.
They keep quiet access, collect information and tunnel data out.
beginner.example: Picture the security booth at the only gate into a factory. Someone replaces the guard's logbook and keeps the original key. Every visitor still gets checked, so nothing looks wrong. But the intruder now reads every delivery note and can walk the site whenever he chooses.
takeaways: Edge appliances need fast patching, because they face the internet directly.
Watch the virtualisation layer, since one flaw there affects many systems.
Logs on the appliance itself are often the only trace of this activity.

objectives: Explain what a zero day vulnerability is and why edge appliances are targeted for it.
Describe why logging on network appliances is critical when endpoint agents cannot be installed.
Summarise the risk of moving from an edge device into a virtualisation platform.
Identify the types of evidence that would indicate tampering on a gateway device.
Explain contested attribution and why cluster names differ between vendors.
